summary: Tsultrim Kelsang works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the International Buddhist Association (attested 1973), Otani University as lecturer (attested 1984) and professor (attested 1999–2002), and Ryukoku University (2015).

Tsuneki Nishiwaki specializes in philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tokyo University of Education (~1962–1970) and held posts at Doshisha University (~1977–1987) and Kyoto University, where he was a professor (~1987–2007).
Tsutomu Hatai worked in Indology and other fields. By 1987, he had succeeded Hiroshi Maruyama and served as president of Ayurveda Kenkyūkai.
Tsutomu Horio specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied under Keiji Nishitani and served as a professor at Otani University (attested 1990).
Tsutomu Kubo was a philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1906–1909) and held an academic post at Tohoku University (~1923–1944).

Tsuyoshi Yokoyama focuses on Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Kyoto University (attested 2015–2017) and held a special appointment as a researcher at the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2017).

Tu Weiming is a scholar of philosophy, Sinology, and religious studies who earned his Ph.D. at Harvard (~1962–1968). He held faculty posts at Princeton, UC Berkeley, Harvard, the Harvard-Yenching Institute, and Peking University.
Tukaram Krishna Laddu worked in Indology and linguistics. He completed studies at the University of Halle-Wittenberg by 1912 and held a post at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1920).

Tulku Sherdor is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Vassar College, Naropa University, and the University of Virginia, learning under Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, Ted Norton, and Jeffrey Hopkins.

Tulku Thondup was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Dodrupchen Monastery under Kyala Khenpo and Khenpo Chemchok, and later served as a visiting scholar at Harvard University.

Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology figure. He studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Dzongsar Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and taught numerous students, including Chokyi Nyima Rinpoche and Tsoknyi Rinpoche.

Turrell V. Wylie was a Tibetologist who studied at the University of Washington (~1950–1958) and under Giuseppe Tucci (~1957–1958). He spent his career at the University of Washington, becoming associate professor (1959) and professor (1970).

Tyler Dewar works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Nitartha Institute (attested 2008, 2019) and trained under Acharya Tashi Wangchuk (2003–2004) and Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche (attested 2019).

Tzungkuen Wen specializes in Buddhist studies and earned a PhD from the University of Queensland (-2009) under Primož Pecenko, Tamara Ditrich, and Chris Kang. He also studied under Yangzhu Xu, Nandasiri Sayadaw, and U Pandita, and lectured at Fuyan Buddhist Institute (2005).

Tōru Funayama works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University and under Ernst Steinkellner (1991–1992), later serving as associate professor at Kyushu University (attested 1999–2003) and professor at Kyoto University (attested 1995–2019).

U Dhammissara is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University (attested 2017), where he studied under Sanu Mahatthanadull and Walmoruwe Piyaratana.
Ugyen Pelgen specializes in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He earned a master's degree from Aligarh Muslim University and served as a lecturer of history at Sherubtse College.

Ulrich Pagel works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied under Tadeusz Skorupski, Philip Denwood, and Renate Söhnen-Thieme, and held a post at SOAS University of London (attested 2013–2020).

Ulrich Timme Kragh is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Copenhagen and Karmapa International Buddhist Institute, later holding posts at Copenhagen, Geumgang University, IIAS, Harvard, University of Sydney, and ANU.

Ulrike Roesler is a scholar of Tibetology and Indology who earned her PhD at the University of Münster. She taught at the universities of Marburg and Freiburg, and became Professor of Tibetan and Himalayan Studies at Oxford (attested 2019).
